newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India drifts mixed as Bombay slips.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India drifts mixed as Bombay slips.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts ended mixed in slow trade on Tuesday following a lacklustre finish in Bombay and amid little fresh news, dealers said.
They said the market was struggling for clear direction amid concern that the key Bombay share index would struggle to break 3,800. It closed Tuesday down 10.01 points at 3,768.30.
ITC lost ground following a decline in Bombay and a later announcement of annual results, which traders in India said were below expectations.
A broker said the market had a firm undertone, with selling limited and buyers still apparent in the quality names.
But a trader said the GDR market had limited upside unless the local market rallied as GDR premiums to local stocks were at high levels.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 0.21 points up at 80.49, with the premium over the local market at 23.36 percent from 22.05 percent.
TELCO added 45 cents to $12.35/13.35, SBI picked up 52 cents to $24.50/25.50 and ITC shed $1.05 to $14.00/15.00.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index lost 1.64 points, or 1.42 percent, to 113.63, representing a discount to the local market of 3.10 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index added 2.07 points to 68.27 points, a premium of 38.20 percent over the local market.
